strengths: Novel and Elegant Architecture Design: The proposed decoupling of the scene representation resolution (viewpoint tokens) from the input image resolution is highly intuitive and effective. It successfully addresses the redundancy issue of pixel-aligned 3D-GS methods.

High Efficiency and Scalability: By replacing full cross-view attention on all image tokens with a two-stage attention mechanism (per-view cross-attention followed by cross-view self-attention on compact viewpoint tokens), the computational complexity is greatly reduced. This allows the model to handle a large number of input views (up to 32 views) without running out of memory.

Superior Experimental Performance: The quantitative and qualitative results on multiple challenging datasets (RE10K, ACID, DL3DV) demonstrate that iLRM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines like MVSplat and DepthSplat. It achieves higher PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS while requiring much lower inference time (often ~5-10x faster) and training memory.

Thorough Ablation Studies: The paper provides comprehensive ablation experiments that isolate and validate each component of the proposed framework, including token uplifting, resolution decoupling, mini-batch cross-attention, and different attention configurations.
weaknesses: Sensitivity to Camera Pose Quality: Like most generalizable feed-forward reconstruction networks, iLRM depends on accurate camera poses. It would be beneficial to discuss or analyze the robustness of the model when the input camera poses are noisy or contain errors, which is common in real-world scenarios.

Spatial Distribution of Gaussians: Since the representation is initialized using viewpoint-centric embeddings tied to specific input cameras, the spatial density and placement of the generated Gaussians are implicitly biased by the input viewpoint distribution. The authors could discuss how this affects scenarios where input cameras are highly clustered or unevenly distributed.

Finetuning Details in Table 5: In the wide-coverage DL3DV experiments (Table 5), the finetuning times for Ours_10 and Ours_50 are incredibly fast (7 seconds and 34 seconds, respectively). A bit more detail on what exactly is updated during this quick finetuning process (e.g., whether it optimizes the Gaussian attributes directly or backpropagates through the network) would clarify this impressive capability.

strengths: The paper introduces a well-motivated architectural design that decouples representation tokens (viewpoint embeddings) from input image tokens, which effectively addresses the high computational cost and redundant Gaussian count of pixel-aligned feed-forward models.

The proposed two-stage attention mechanism (per-view cross-attention followed by global self-attention over compact representation tokens) and the token uplifting strategy allow the model to ingest high-resolution visual cues while keeping the computational footprint highly manageable.

The experimental results are very strong. iLRM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods like DepthSplat and MVSplat in terms of rendering quality (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) while being substantially faster and using much less memory.
The paper is very well-written, with clear explanations of the architectural choices and a comprehensive set of ablation studies validating each component of the proposed method.
weaknesses: The claim of 'feedback-driven iterative refinement' is somewhat overstated. Architecturally, the model is a standard feed-forward transformer with stacked layers (12 layers) using unshared weights, rather than a recurrent loop or a true iterative optimization that renders intermediate states and feeds back residuals. The connection to optimization is more of a conceptual metaphor than an explicit recurrency or feedback loop.

While training memory and iteration speeds are provided, the total training cost in terms of GPU-hours or days for a full training run from scratch is not clearly documented, which would be helpful for understanding the overall training complexity.

strengths: Clear motivation and elegant architecture design. Decoupling the scene representation from input image resolutions addresses a critical computational and memory bottleneck in feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) reconstruction.

The two-stage attention mechanism (per-view cross-attention followed by cross-view self-attention over low-resolution viewpoint embeddings) scales much more efficiently than traditional full-attention over all multi-view image tokens.

Extremely strong empirical performance. The proposed iLRM consistently and significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods (such as DepthSplat and MVSplat) across standard datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID) in terms of rendering quality (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS), while producing more compact Gaussian representations and running significantly faster.

Comprehensive evaluation and ablation studies, which thoroughly validate all the key design choices (e.g., iterative refinement layers, token uplifting, mini-batch cross-attention schemes, and initialization methods).
weaknesses: The framing of the architecture as 'iterative refinement' is slightly overstated, as the layers do not share weights recurrently. Instead, it is a standard deep feed-forward transformer stack with separate parameters per layer.

Like most current feed-forward generalizable reconstruction pipelines, the method remains highly sensitive to camera pose accuracy, and its performance under noisy or estimated poses is not extensively explored.

strengths: Elegant and physically intuitive design that mimics iterative optimization inside a feed-forward transformer framework using layer-by-layer cross-attention updates.

Outstanding efficiency and scalability. By decoupling viewpoint embeddings from input image resolution and decomposing global attention into a two-stage scheme, the model dramatically reduces computational complexity and memory consumption, avoiding out-of-memory errors on large numbers of input views where baseline methods fail.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across multiple diverse datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID, Tanks & Temples, Mip-NeRF360), showing clear superiority in rendering quality, speed, and geometric fidelity.

Thorough ablation studies that carefully validate each individual contribution, including the iterative refinement mechanism, resolution decoupling, token uplifting, and mini-batch attention strategies.
Excellent qualitative analysis and visualization of attention maps, which beautifully demonstrate the progressive convergence of cross-view correspondences as the layers deepen.
weaknesses: While compact viewpoint embeddings alleviate the computational burden, the self-attention mechanism across all viewpoint tokens still scales quadratically with the number of input views, which may become a bottleneck for extremely large-scale scene captures.
The method still relies on accurate camera poses and is restricted to static scenarios, although this is a common limitation of current generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting methods.

The reconstructed 3D geometry, while better than existing feed-forward baselines, still lags slightly behind methods that employ explicit geometric supervision, since the model is trained purely with rendering losses.

strengths: Innovative design that decouples the 3D Gaussian representation from the input image resolution. This allows the model to generate highly compact Gaussian representations while still utilizing high-resolution image guidance.

The proposed two-stage attention mechanism (localized per-view cross-attention followed by global viewpoint self-attention) elegantly addresses the quadratic computational complexity of multi-view transformers.

Exceptional quantitative performance. The model significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art feed-forward methods (e.g., DepthSplat, GS-LRM, Long-LRM) on RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, while requiring a fraction of the inference time and memory.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation, including not only novel view synthesis but also depth estimation consistency, geometry estimation (Chamfer Distance and F1-score on NRGBD/ETH3D), camera pose noise robustness, and scaling capabilities up to 256 input views.

Outstanding supplementary material containing thorough ablation studies (validating self-attention role, group-attention, initialization schemes, and token uplifting) and intuitive attention visualizations that validate the iterative feedback concept.
weaknesses: The core transformer blocks (alternating cross-attention and self-attention layers) borrow concepts from existing architectures such as Perceiver and VGGT, though their adaptation to 3D Gaussian generation is highly specialized and effective.

The framework relies heavily on accurate camera poses (encoded as Plücker coordinates) and lacks joint pose optimization or refinement, which could limit applicability on in-the-wild phone-captured videos with noisy poses.

With 185M parameters, the model is significantly larger than some lightweight pixel-aligned models (e.g., MVSplat at 12M), which could be a consideration for edge device deployment, although its runtime efficiency and lower Gaussian count offset this in overall systems.

strengths: The paper addresses a highly relevant bottleneck in feed-forward 3D reconstruction models (specifically large 3D reconstruction models like GS-LRM/Long-LRM): the quadratic computational complexity in relation to both view count and image resolution.

The proposed architectural design—specifically decoupling viewpoint representations from input image resolution and decomposing multi-view interaction into per-view cross-attention and global self-attention—is logical, well-motivated, and highly effective.

The token uplifting strategy and mini-batch cross-attention schemes successfully allow the model to ingest high-resolution image cues while generating lightweight, compact 3D Gaussian representations.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (RE10K, ACID, DL3DV, Tanks&Temples, Mip-NeRF360) demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency (training and inference speed, memory usage). It scales up to 256 views without running out of memory.

The qualitative visualizations, particularly the attention maps over transformer layers (Figure 8 & 18), are highly insightful and convincingly show that the model learns physically consistent geometric correspondences as the refinement progresses.
weaknesses: The concept of 'iterative refinement' is implemented as standard stacked feed-forward transformer layers (a standard deep network). While the interpretation of this process as implicit gradient updates under static image evidence is intriguing, it does not actually run a classic optimization loop with rendering feedback.

The model relies heavily on accurate camera poses (via Plücker coordinates) as inputs. When poses are noisy or unavailable, performance may degrade significantly, which limits its applicability to in-the-wild or uncalibrated image collections.
